# Supabase staging test plan

Status: PLAN ONLY. No SQL, project creation, connection to production, migration, React deployment or test execution is authorized by this document. Obtain separate execution authorization. Static parsing is not an integration-test result.

## Step 0: empty staging bootstrap (new approved target, execution NOT authorized)

Staging inventory-app-staging already exists; allowed reference is qowhwyiooxxvdbnerlpa.
Do not create another project or connect under this documentation-only task. For this empty
staging, use STAGING_BOOTSTRAP.sql and STAGING_BOOTSTRAP_REVIEW.md before 001. Separately create
three synthetic Auth users via staging Dashboard/API (never SQL auth.users inserts), fill the
NULL project/marker/UUID inputs in an approved execution copy, independently verify destination,
then run the whole bootstrap only after execution approval. Missing inputs abort before seed.
Expected counts are 3 profiles, 4 materials, 5 models, 6 BOM rows, 6 fully-picked requests and
0 stock logs. Automatic flag setup occurs via RPC after 004; bootstrap contains legacy columns
only. This supersedes the schema-export requirement below for this minimal rehearsal, not for
production-fidelity testing. No signup trigger is installed because managed auth schema must
remain untouched; signup-trigger test is BLOCKED in this fixture, not passing by assumption.

## Isolated environment and schema provenance

1. The existing separately created inventory-app-staging project is the target; do not provision another project. A project administrator verifies it with its own project reference, database password, API credentials and test-only Auth users. Use a separate staging web origin/browser profile. Record the allowed staging project reference and URL in the run sheet; stop if the destination does not match it. Do not link an automatic production deploy or merge workflow.
2. Use an already supplied, reviewed schema-only export/artifact. There is no authorization to dump or connect to production now. If the artifact is unavailable, ask the owner to supply it through an approved channel; do not infer missing legacy definitions from React. Validate public tables, columns, keys, grants, policies, index definition, is_admin and signup-profile trigger against the audit before replaying the four drafts. Fresh Supabase provides its managed Auth schemas: do not restore production auth.users, auth credentials or managed internal schemas wholesale.
3. Review even schema-only artifacts for embedded webhook endpoints, function literals, role passwords and credentials. Keep private artifacts and credentials out of repository, screenshots, logs, CSV and this document. Use the deployment secret store or protected local environment; never embed database/service credentials in command lines or VITE variables. The client only receives its staging URL and publishable/anon key, with real staging user sessions. Use the existing variable names VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.
4. Seed synthetic materials/models/BOM/orders, not copied customer names, emails, order references or stock history. Create test Auth accounts using staging Auth and record their generated UUIDs; set test roles through authorized staging administration. Do not copy production password hashes, tokens, profiles or real staff identities. Leave Sheets webhook blank; disable outbound integrations/email to real recipients.
5. If a Supabase branch is chosen instead, explicitly choose schema-only/no production data and prohibit merge to production. A separate project is the default here because no production connection is allowed. Branch creation and availability are separate operator decisions.

Official references checked for planning: [Managing environments](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/managing-environments), [Branching](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/branching), [CLI workflow](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/cli-workflows). CLI dump supports schema exports, but do not run a production pull/dump or remote reset under this plan. Provisioning details should be rechecked at execution time.

## Fixtures and run evidence

Use admin A, admin B, staff S1, staff S2, purchasing P, plus anonymous and expired-session clients. API permission tests use their real JWTs, never SQL Editor postgres/service-role as a substitute for user authorization. Privileged staging inspection is only for the independent oracle.

Prepare legacy materials M1/M2 (manual, 100 each), M3 (automatic, 100), zero-stock M0, decimals such as 0.25, and two distinct UUIDs sharing the same name/unit. Legacy requires_picking defaults true; set selected test automatic flags through the new RPC after activation. Models: CIEM C1/C2, Lifestyle L1/L2, Sleepplug S, Tactical T; manual-only, mixed and auto-only BOM variants. Use repair mode for repair requests with reasons. Use independent fixtures for each test to avoid stock/order contamination.

Prepare synthetic fully-picked legacy requests, including received=false and no log, with no requires_picking flag. A 138 received/198 unreceived fixture may reproduce the old distribution but must not copy production identities. Legacy pending/malformed/collision fixtures belong in disposable negative-test clones, not the passing cutover fixture. Baseline is current observed stock, not inferred old usage.

For each case record case ID, migration/artifact hashes, stage reference, actor role/test UUID, operation/request IDs, input sans tokens, expected/actual result, before/after quantities and versions, relevant movements/allocations/cancellations/stocktakes and duration. Mark NOT RUN/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED individually. Preserve error code/message without authorization headers. Never mark a case passing from HTTP status alone.

## Deployment order and phase gates

| Phase | Action after separate approval | Required gate | Failure/recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bootstrap (empty staging) | Execute reviewed STAGING_BOOTSTRAP.sql with verified staging marker and test Auth UUIDs | Exact schema/index/role baseline, no production endpoints | Discard/recreate the disposable staging project from the approved artifact |
| 001 additive | Apply 001 as expected migration owner | 8 new tables, flags default true, legacy quantities unchanged; old policies remain; capture before/after schema | Failed transaction rolls back; inspect cause. If applied, retain compatible additions or manually reverse unused new objects after dependency review |
| 002 RPC | Apply 002 | Function owners/search_path/ACL and digests correct; mutation RPCs reject inactive cutover with no writes | Failed transaction rolls back. Do not edit digest/control to bypass failures; restore the unused staging fixture if needed |
| New React deploy | Build/deploy the future approved app to staging with new mutation controls disabled | New build reaches staging only; no direct-write fallback; PWA old tabs tested | Roll back UI before cutover only while legacy behavior is still permitted |
| Maintenance and 003 | Stop writers, drain in-flight operations, retire old PWA tabs, review exact manifest/actor/operation/note/legacy-return choice, then apply 003 | Cancel window -1; no pending legacy work; exact index/dependencies; no live normalized collisions. Baseline equals qty without opening movement; lookup index replaces old unique index; phase 3 frozen | Any preflight or later error must leave phase 2, old index and no baseline changes. After successful 003 keep freeze if later work fails; never reopen legacy writers casually |
| 004 hardening | Apply 004 after phase-3 verification | Schema/RPC digests match; direct API writes denied; phase 4 active; all role/integrity checks | On failure phase-3 freeze persists. Investigate or recreate staging; after new ledger writes prefer forward fix or consistent full staging restore |
| Acceptance | Enable staged UI, run all cases below and inspect old/new clients | No partial stock events, secret exposure, unauthorized access or missing report rows | Block promotion on any unexplained failure |

Baseline approval fields are intentionally unresolved in the drafts. Fill only a reviewed staging execution copy with staging values when authorized. Do not change production drafts to fake test approval. For index rollback after 003, keep freeze and recheck original uniqueness before restoring: repair repeats/cancelled-key reuse may prevent restoration. Never delete transactions merely to make the unique index fit. Capture backup/artifact before every phase; no generic automatic down after ledger writes.

## Every public RPC: positive and negative tests

Each mutator also runs the replay, role-denial and rollback cases below.

| ID / RPC | Positive expectation | Negative/boundary expectation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R01 inventory_create_material | Admin creates zero and nonzero initial stock; defaults active/manual; zero baseline plus exactly one opening movement only for nonzero | Staff/P denied; blank name/unit, negative/nonfinite qty rejected; no orphan material/baseline/operation |
| R02 inventory_update_material | Admin changes name, threshold including zero, flag; qty/version unchanged | Unit change rejected; stale client qty cannot be submitted; missing ID and invalid threshold rejected |
| R03 inventory_set_material_active | Admin archives/reactivates; history retained | Unpicked line of that material in uncancelled request blocks; a picked line with another material pending does NOT block; other roles denied |
| R04 inventory_receive_purchase | Admin/P receive positive decimal qty, movement before/after and actor match | Staff denied; zero/negative/nonfinite, inactive/missing material rejected; no partial change |
| R05 inventory_stocktake | Admin submits counted quantity and current version; positive/negative delta logged; equal count records stocktake without movement | Staff/P denied; stale version rejects; changed count requires reason; negative/nonfinite count rejected |
| R06 inventory_create_request | Admin/S1 request server model BOM; flags/name/category/actor from server; auto-only completes atomically | P denied; invalid model/BOM/inactive material/empty repair BOM/blank repair note rejected; no trusted client picked/role/name override |
| R07 inventory_confirm_pick | Admin exact transaction/line UUID batch; manual lines issue; final manual completion issues automatic lines once | Staff/P denied; missing/cancelled request, wrong line UUID and selecting automatic line fail; all items roll back |
| R08 inventory_cancel_request | Staff owns unissued request indefinitely; admin cancels issued and returns exact outstanding allocations | Other staff/P denied; picked flag OR any allocation forbids staff even net-zero; reason required; no duplicate return |
| R09 inventory_save_model | Admin creates/updates model/BOM in one operation; old request snapshots unchanged | Other roles denied; malformed/empty BOM or invalid material/qty rolls back model and BOM; no client model delete fallback |
| R10 inventory_list_materials | Admin/P see current stock/version; staff sees active catalog without qty/version/threshold | Anonymous denied; staff include_inactive does not expose archived rows or stock |
| R11 inventory_list_my_requests | Staff sees own only, admin all; cancelled marker and workflow_state correct; old picked/unreceived completed | P denied; cursor tuple incomplete/invalid limit rejected; traverse >1000 rows without loss |
| R12 inventory_list_pick_queue | Admin sees only unpicked manual snapshot lines, stable line UUIDs and no cancelled requests | Staff/P denied; automatic-only/completed absent; page boundary/equal timestamps no duplicates |
| R13 inventory_balance_report | Admin/P correct dates, coverage, totals and repair split over >1000 transactions | Staff denied; invalid timezone/range rejected; pre-cutover opening/closing NULL, not invented zero |
| R15 inventory_set_model_active | Admin archives/reactivates with reason, operation audit and pending_request_count | Staff/P denied; null flag, blank reason, missing UUID fail; history/qty unchanged |
| R14 inventory_list_movements | Admin/P fixed sequence cutoff, material/date filters, allocations; all pages export | Staff denied; invalid limit/cutoff/date range rejected; later inserts excluded from original cutoff |

## Business rules and snapshot cases

O01: CIEM C1 order ABC then C2 order ' abc ' succeeds; repeat C1 rejects. O02: each of Lifestyle/Sleepplug/Tactical rejects overlap with any normal category including CIEM in both insertion orders. O03: multiple repairs use ABC successfully with separate operation UUIDs and nonblank notes, regardless of normal request ABC. O04: repair blank/space note rejects, including model-mode repair with no note input. O05: cancellation releases normal key; completion alone does not. O06: UUID identity survives equal order refs; no stage field. O07: new unknown category rejects in create RPC; legacy unknown/null non-repair category is conservatively normal for collision preflight.

In separate phase-2 clones, create lower/trim collisions, cross-category collisions and allowed CIEM different-model/repair examples before maintenance. 003 must reject each collision before DROP, leaving old index/phase/baseline unchanged. Cancelled fixtures are excluded. Hold the table/advisory locks while a second writer attempts an insert: it must wait and then fail the phase-3 write guard; no insertion in the validation/cutover gap. Schema alteration/index dependency/manifest mismatch variants must fail closed without manual digest edits.

Change materials.requires_picking after creating a pending request: the old snapshot remains unchanged, a new request adopts the new flag. Old missing flags mean true regardless of unit. For mixed M1/M2/manual and M3/automatic, first manual issue must not issue M3; last manual confirmation must issue M3 in the same transaction. An auto-only request issues all on creation and never requires recheck.

## Atomic failure, replay and concurrency

A01 insufficient stock: arrange one selected material with enough stock and a later UUID-sorted material short. Submit one multi-line confirm operation. Expect no qty/version/BOM/movement/allocation/operation result changes for ANY selected material or request. Repeat with final-manual mixed operation where automatic stock is short, and auto-only creation where one material is short (no request should survive).

A02 movement failure: in a disposable active staging clone only, an authorized tester temporarily introduces a narrowly targeted fault trigger that raises on a chosen later movement insert, after an earlier material has been processed. Fault fixture implementation needs separate SQL review/authorization; none is included or installed now. Do not disable production integrity triggers or bypass errors. Submit through a real actor session, inspect that every earlier change and operation row rolled back, remove only the test fault, verify schema matches the recorded post-004 fixture, and retry. Also inject an allocation/commit-time constraint failure to check deferred errors reach the client, not a false success. Apply fault/replay checks to purchase, stocktake, opening create, issue and cancellation return; no fixture changes between 001 and digest-gated cutover.

A03 idempotency: for each mutation, submit the exact operation UUID/actor/kind/payload twice sequentially and concurrently. Same stored result, one effect only. Same UUID with changed payload, actor or RPC kind rejects. Simulate response loss after server commit, retry exact request and verify no second effect. Known failed/rolled-back operation can retry original payload; changed business intent uses a new UUID only after resolving the original outcome. Different UUID must not reissue picked lines or duplicate cancellation returns.

A04 contention: admins A/B concurrently issue 7 from M1=10 for distinct requests. Exactly one succeeds and one rejects insufficient stock, final qty=3 and one set of allocations. Reset fixture for 4+4: both succeed, final qty=2 with contiguous versions. Include purchase versus pick, stocktake versus purchase (stale version rejects), cancel versus pick (serialized valid result, no double return), and opposite-order multi-material batches (no lost updates/deadlock). Record commits and lock waits, not browser timing assumptions.

## Cancellation, security and history

Staff cancellation older than 30 minutes/days succeeds only for own unpicked/unallocated request; any picked legacy flag denies even without logs. Admin issue+cancel returns once and retains request/cancellation audit. Legacy return mode blocked rejects issued legacy cancellation; test admin_verified in a separately approved baseline fixture with explicit physical verification. No automatic backfill or inferred return. Existing 198 picked/unreceived fixtures display completed without changed JSON.

For every RPC run allowed and denied role sessions; anonymous/expired/missing profile denied. After 004 attempt direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for materials, transactions/BOM flags, stock_log, model/BOM, private ledger and role escalation: denied and row counts unchanged. Staff cannot read others or stock via direct tables/views/RPC, P cannot create/pick/cancel/stocktake. Direct helper calls denied. Verify new RPC SECURITY DEFINER empty search_path, full qualification and grants; no API role membership in inventory_executor. Verify profile signup still works. Check app_settings/Sheets separately: not governed by these inventory migrations; do not assume it was hardened.

## Report oracle and acceptance

Use a complete post-cutover day, not cutover midnight (a midday cutover must return before_coverage for that day). Synthetic baseline M1=100; purchase +20, normal issue -10, repair issue -3, normal cancellation return +10, repair return +3, count 115 (adjustment -5). Expect opening=100, purchase=20, issue=13, returned=13, production_issue=10, repair_issue=3, production_returned=10, repair_returned=3, adjustment_out=5, closing=115. Next complete day opening=115. Run independent +adjustment, zero count, zero-delta count, decimal and new-material opening cases. Pre-existing baseline has NO opening movement; a new material zero baseline and optional opening movement count once. Missing baseline/pre-coverage yields explicit NULL coverage. Verify Bangkok midnight boundaries, archived materials and immutable name/unit history. Cancellation events remain dated returns even though cancelled requests no longer count as live BOM demand.

CSV must match all report columns and all sequence-cutoff pages, including >2000 movements; use safe synthetic text containing commas/newlines and spreadsheet formula prefixes. Never sum repair breakdowns on top of total issue/returned. Current request-summary RPC lacks a server date/report aggregate; see React plan gaps before promising a complete production-count report for purchasing.

PASS only when all required role/RPC cases and invariants have evidence: qty never negative; material version/ledger chain contiguous; allocations sum to issue/return movement; no orphan/unfinalized committed operation; rollback snapshots equal; replay one effect; cancelled-key behavior correct; report reconciles; no unauthorized reads/writes. Any failure blocks activation/promotion. No tests have been run by preparing this plan. Future React acceptance runs available npm run build and npm run lint (no test script exists), plus the integration cases above; build success alone is insufficient.
## Read-result regression cases — latest 002 draft

Q01: R11/R12 return model_id/model_name/category/note from transactions. After current-model
rename/reclassification/BOM edit, history/queue preserve original metadata. Repair model_id
NULL and reason remain visible. Verify all pages, permissions and cursors unchanged.
Q02: mixed three-line BOM (two manual, one automatic): counts total/picked/pending/manual
pending = 3/0/3/2, queue lines length 2. First manual picked => 3/1/2/1, partially_picked.
Last manual plus auto issue => 3/3/0/0, completed in history and absent in queue.
Q03: missing flag means true regardless of unit. All picked but received=false => completed.
Cancelled status wins even if picked complete; retain counts, exclude from queue. Empty
legacy BOM yields zero counts and existing completed behavior; do not backfill snapshots.
Q04: verify total_lines=picked_lines+pending_lines and queue lines length equals
pending_picking_lines. SQL parsing is not proof of API behavior; all cases NOT RUN now.

## Model lifecycle cases — implemented in drafts, NOT RUN

M01: models.is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true preserves old/new model availability.
inventory_save_model creates/edits without changing old transactions; editing inactive model
must not reactivate it. No historical quantity/snapshot/movement updates.
M02: inventory_set_model_active(operation UUID,model UUID,boolean,reason) is admin
only; staff/purchasing/anonymous denied; null flag, blank reason, missing model rejected.
Exact retry one effect; changed actor/payload rejects; operation audit and rollback tested.
M03: archived model rejects NEW create_request despite stale UI; reactivation permits it
subject to normal order rules. History readable; existing pending request can complete or
cancel. Returned pending_request_count warns without blocking archive.
M04: concurrent archive/create serialized on writer/model lock; no creation when archive
wins first. No model DELETE endpoint; direct client deletion after hardening denied,
including history-referenced model. Legacy additive policies remain until maintenance.
M05: repeat clean 001-004 rehearsal for the 15-RPC draft; verify new column, ACLs and digests. All model cases remain NOT RUN until staging execution is separately authorized.

Role editing in the app is excluded from this release and deferred to later system
administration. Continue role escalation-denial/signup tests; do not assume a new role
management RPC/UI or use profile updates from the client as a test setup shortcut.

M06: one pending transaction with three pending lines counts as 1, two pending transactions
as 2. Cancelled and fully-picked/unreceived requests count as 0. Partial and automatic-pending
lines count as unfinished work. Capture exact history/BOM hashes before/after toggles and edits.
M07: retry original toggle after pending count changes: same operation returns its persisted
count and produces no second mutation. New operation with same desired state still requires
reason; previous_is_active and current flag agree. Request replay after archive returns original
success, while a fresh operation UUID attempting new creation rejects.
M08: race archive with create/pick/cancel/edit; original pending requests continue, edited inactive
models remain inactive, and no historical model/category/note/BOM fields change. Verify 004 denies
API update of is_active, including column-level grants; executor has only existing authorized
model writes, no DELETE grant. Existing schema/RPC digest gates must detect unexpected edits.

## PostgreSQL 17.6 ownership transfer — corrected managed baseline contract

Runtime evidence supplied by the user: the automatic inventory_executor -> postgres edge
has grantor supabase_admin, ADMIN=true, INHERIT=false, SET=false. The previous zero-member
postflight raised P0001 after ownership transfer; rollback restored this expected baseline.

002 now requires exactly this one direct row before AND after ownership transfer, including
its grantor. Extra rows (including grantor postgres), wrong flags or missing baseline abort.
API roles anon/authenticated/service_role must have no direct or indirect executor membership.
Temporary GRANT inventory_executor TO postgres WITH SET TRUE and subsequent REVOKE remain
inside the same transaction. No INHERIT is enabled; NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS remain
required. Errors restore the original baseline and roll back DDL/phase/ACL changes together.
Function ownership remains inventory_executor; inv_schema_digest stays postgres as before.

RPC_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION.sql now has six read-only SELECT/WITH SELECT statements: query 2
shows membership paths/flags/grantors, 2b verifies exact direct baseline and API exclusion.
Other queries cover owners, role attributes, RPC grants and phase. Static parsing does not
prove managed GRANT/REVOKE permission or runtime operator resolution. The user now reports
002 runtime verification passed: phase=2 inactive, correct owners, 15 authenticated-only
public RPCs and the exact managed baseline. 004 runtime verification remains NOT RUN.

Regression cases for separately authorized staging: exact baseline passes; zero rows, wrong
grantor/flags, extra postgres-granted row or API membership fail. Successful 002 must preserve
baseline exactly and remove temporary SET membership. Injected failure must restore phase 1
and original memberships/functions/ACLs. Confirm 16 public RPC grants and phase 2 inactive.

004_hardening.sql now verifies the same exact managed baseline in both preflight and
postflight, including grantor/flags, API direct/indirect membership exclusion and executor
NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS. It does not grant SET or INHERIT or alter membership.
No permanent schema objects or grants added by this correction. 002 statement/body counts
are now 113/32 after recovery; entire fresh migration suite contains 39 procedural bodies. Read-only runtime query
count increases from five to six. No SQL was executed or Supabase connection made here.


## 004 baseline alignment verification

The previous 004 had a blanket membership preflight and no membership postflight. Both
boundaries now require exactly one direct inventory_executor membership: postgres granted
by supabase_admin, admin=true, inherit=false, set=false. Any absent/extra/wrong row rejects;
API roles are additionally checked for indirect membership. Unsafe executor attributes reject.
No changes to 001-003, role flags, membership grants, function owners or schema objects.
Existing transaction/advisory lock and final activation remain; postflight runs before phase=4.

Staging cases (not executed here): approved baseline passes; missing row, wrong grantor,
extra member, changed admin/inherit/set flag, indirect API membership, LOGIN/SUPERUSER/
BYPASSRLS each fail. After success repeat runtime queries and expect phase=4 active with
baseline unchanged. A failure must retain phase 3 inactive and its maintenance freeze.
Test on isolated approved fixtures; do not weaken earlier digest checks to reach a test.
Static counts stay 23 top-level statements/4 procedural bodies for 004; no object-count change.

## Recovery RPC and replay acceptance (new, NOT RUN)

Deployment: fresh staging uses updated 002 (16 RPCs); the existing phase=2 inactive
staging uses 002A only after separate approval. Do not rerun 002. Before patch,
record the current digest and the sole postgres/supabase_admin baseline grant
(admin=true, inherit=false, set=false). Wrong phase, active=true, schema/RPC drift,
existing lookup, other memberships/grantors/flags must abort. Force a failure in a
separate disposable test copy after owner transfer and verify full rollback of RPC,
digest and temporary privileges. Success retains phase 2 inactive and only baseline
membership; run the read-only RPC_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION.sql separately. No 003/004
execution is authorized here.

Use real synthetic authenticated sessions (never postgres as the RLS oracle):

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Own operation: staff/admin/purchasing | Exactly found, kind, completed, result, created_at, completed_at; no payload |
| Other actor: staff/purchasing | Same full JSON as nonexistent UUID |
| Admin assisting other actor | Result readable without changing actor/data |
| Anonymous/service_role/PUBLIC | No EXECUTE grant; null auth.uid rejected |
| Committed mutation, response dropped, reload | Lookup uses existing UUID, displays original result, deletes replay; mutation count unchanged |
| Found incomplete | Wait/check only; same UUID, no new mutation |
| Not found | No automatic replay on reload; explicit retry sends identical arguments and UUID |
| In-flight uncommitted mutation invisible to lookup | Retry with same UUID serializes at server; only one operation/movement set commits |
| Account switch during lookup or before retry | Old controller stops, other namespace absent; no other-user replay |
| Corrupt JSON/fingerprint/secret-shaped payload | Fail closed, preserve evidence, no new UUID/network mutation |
| Pending older than 7 days | Still recoverable; no expiry deletion |
| Storage unavailable | Visible memory warning; same-session retry safe; do not claim reload durability |
| Lookup network failure | Recheck button available; no mutation fallback |
| Repeated clicks | Single in-flight lookup/replay for that UUID |

A normally committed operation cannot remain incomplete because deferred integrity
checks require finalization; test incomplete UI via mocks and in-flight visibility
with two staging sessions rather than disabling production constraints. Database
concurrency, ACL, rollback and browser UX checks are not covered by local parser tests.

Pass only if ledger/log counts, stock and returned result prove one committed action
and no unauthorized result disclosure. On failure keep V2 disabled, preserve pending
records and evidence; do not delete operations or rerun with fresh UUIDs. Do not drop
lookup after clients depend on it without a separately reviewed rollback plan.
